V3. NOT a "could not check == checked and found nothing" defect, which I went looking for specifically. lwb_lanes.commit_files runs git diff-tree with check=True, so an unreadable or bogus sha raises CalledProcessError and the gate dies loudly rather than returning an empty file list that would read as a clean pass. And _is_record_only_commit returns False on an empty file list, so a merge commit (diff-tree prints nothing for one) is NOT record-only and stays subject to the identity check. The exemption is fail-CLOSED on both paths. I confirmed the merge case on a scratch repo.

V4. The exemption is correctly narrow with respect to CODE. An impostor-authored commit touching a script, or mixing a script with a reviews/ file, is still rejected by lwb-commit-identity -- the all() over changed files means one non-record file re-arms the check. Directive 10 is intact for anything that changes code.

B2. 187 LINES OF THE MERGE GATE'S RECORDED RATIONALE WERE DESTROYED BY A PLACEHOLDER ROUND-TRIP AND NEVER RESTORED, AND THE PR BODY DOES NOT MENTION IT. Measured, not estimated:
    git show 54eb044:scripts/lwb_lanes.py  ->  the single word "placeholder", 0 newline-terminated lines.
    main 845 lines / 180 comment tokens; this head 658 lines / 102 comment tokens; delta -187 lines, -78 comments.
    Unicode em dashes in the file: 9 on main, 2 here.
So 54eb044 overwrote the whole file with a placeholder, 3f6a2b5 put back a reconstruction, and the reconstruction is 187 lines short. Combined with V1 (the executable code is byte-for-byte identical bar two lines), the signature is unmistakable: the file was re-uploaded from a model's reconstruction, not edited. The em-dash-to-double-hyphen conversion across the whole file is the tell. What was lost is not decoration -- it includes the note explaining why a commit with NO files is not record-only, which is precisely the property that makes THIS PR's own exemption safe on merge commits (V3), and the recorded reasoning behind the vendor-agnostic review rule and the pr-field reconciliation, each of which exists because an adversarial review found a hole. A commit titled "document the record-only exemption" whose net effect is -187 lines of documentation is a quantitative claim contradicted by its own diff. The fix is mechanical: apply the two functional lines to `git show e5f29bf:scripts/lwb_lanes.py`.

B3. THE RECORD-ONLY EXEMPTION REACHES THE FILES THAT DEFINE THE GATES, NOT JUST BOOKKEEPING. _is_record_only_commit tests the DIRECTORY prefixes "reviews/" and "proof/", which contain reviews/schema.json, proof/schema.json and proof/exempt.json -- the definitions lwb_lanes.py and lwb_check_proof.py enforce against. Reproduced on a scratch clone of this head; I did not assert this from reading:
    commit as "Impostor Dev <impostor@example.com>" changing ONLY reviews/schema.json, setting its required[] to []
    -> scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py (this branch): "lwb-commit-identity check passed"  EXIT 0
    -> scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py (main's version, same commit): "FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare..."  EXIT 1
    -> lwb_lanes.resolve_reviewable_head skips it: raw head b84522f, reviewable head 4793afc
So a commit that guts the review-record schema is, on this branch, authored by anyone, exempt from the identity gate, and skipped by the reviewable-head walk, meaning no review record need ever name it. main rejects that same commit. Narrow the predicate to per-PR records -- reviews/<n>/*.json and proof/<n>.json -- rather than the whole directories. This finding matches the one reviewer B filed as F5; I reproduced it independently and my repro is above.

C1. CONTEXT, EXPLICITLY NOT CHARGED TO THIS PR. independent_reviews never compares a record's self-declared commit_author_id against the actual author of commit_sha; it globs reviews/<pr>/*.json once and the same record set satisfies every shared-touching commit in the range. A reviewer's own record therefore authorizes the reviewer's own record-only commit. I verified this is TRUE ON MAIN TOO and is untouched by this diff, so it is pre-existing and not this PR's to answer for. I raise it only because the record-only exemption in B3 makes the surface it applies to larger. reviews/README.md already says the identity fields are self-attested and unverified; this is the mechanical consequence of that, recorded, not charged.
